capabilities: note-taking | Stores hierarchical notes in a tree, with rich-text, Markdown, code, canvas and other note types, attributes, scripting and a web interface.
description:
UnitySVC runs the official TriliumNext Notes image in a separate container for each enrollment, with its own HTTPS address. Trilium is a self-hosted note-taking application for large personal knowledge bases: notes are arranged in a tree (a note can sit in several places), and can be rich text, Markdown, code, maps, canvases and more, with attributes, relations, note history, full-text search, scripting and a web clipper. Everything is kept in the instance's own SQLite database, stored in the `trilium` folder of your home, so it survives stopping the instance and even removing it and enrolling again.

Enroll in the base channel, then open the instance address straight away: Trilium has no environment setting for its password, so the first visitor to the address chooses it. Set a strong password immediately, then log in. You can run one Trilium instance at a time. See How to use this service for full setup and limitations.

You pay the selected channel's platform compute cost while the instance runs, including idle time, and the platform keeps the data in your home while it is stopped. Labs adds no markup and receives no seller payout. See the upstream Trilium documentation and issue tracker for software-specific help.
